overview.summary: Expanse EDU leverages evidence-based psychology principles to drive student engagement, motivation, and learning

dopamine.title: Dopamine & Motivation
dopamine.description: Dopamine is the primary determinant of how motivated we are, how excited we are, how outward facing we are, and how willing we are to lean into life and pursue things.

keyInsights.insight: Dopamine increases in anticipation of reward
keyInsights.application: Expanse's reward system leverages anticipation to improve mood and motivation

keyInsights.insight: Dopamine is a universal currency for moving us towards goals
keyInsights.application: Using dopamine mechanics to drive academic goal achievement

keyInsights.insight: Our experience of life depends on dopamine relative to recent experience
keyInsights.application: Designing reward schedules that maintain healthy dopamine levels

rewardVariance.concept: Intermittent reward schedules are highly engaging
rewardVariance.application: Variable rewards (sometimes small, sometimes large) maintain engagement without dopamine depletion

positiveReinforcement.title: Positive Reinforcement
positiveReinforcement.description: Positive reinforcement encourages repeating good behaviors, builds confidence, and develops positive motivation for success.

benefits.detail: Feeling safe at school improves academic performance because children feel connected to teachers and peers in a supportive environment
Teachers using positive reinforcement feel they're making progress, leading to more pleasant and rewarding teaching experiences
PBIS can lead to 20-40% reduction in disciplinary referrals, including suspensions and expulsions

pbisEvidence.impact: Frees up valuable instructional time and creates a more positive learning environment

disparityData.issue: Black students are 3.6 times more likely to be suspended out of school compared to white students
disparityData.expanseRole: Positive reinforcement systems can help reduce bias-driven punishment disparities

adultificationBias.description: Black girls, in particular, may face 'adultification bias' where they are viewed as older and more mature than their age, leading to harsher punishments

socialDevelopment.title: Social Development

insights.finding: Children spend far less time in embodied social behaviors essential for development
Overprotection in real world and underprotection in virtual world are major reasons for anxious generation
After-school hours were probably more valuable for social development and mental health than anything in school (other than recess)
Children who are routinely exposed to small risks grow up to handle much larger risks without panicking

socialDevelopment.socialValidation: As children begin puberty, they are often socially insecure, easily swayed by peer pressure, and easily lured by any activity that seems to offer social validation

selfEfficacy.title: Self-Efficacy
selfEfficacy.definition: Individual's belief in their capacity to execute behaviors necessary to produce specific performance attainments
keyPrinciples: Help students set clear and specific goals
Students who set goals experience initial sense of self-efficacy and commit to persist
Asking students what rewards they want to achieve encourages goal-setting
Rewards equal goals in the self-efficacy framework
instructionalPractices: Encourage students to set clear, specific, and challenging proximal goals
Provide students with honest and explicit feedback
selfEfficacy.source: Academic Self-Efficacy: From Educational Theory to Instructional Practice (NCBI)

learningAndAttention.principle: Learning and memory are direct consequences of attentional processing
learningAndAttention.detail: The more attention is directed toward something, the more likely it is to be learned and remembered
learningAndAttention.application: Gamification captures attention, thereby improving learning outcomes

brainDevelopment.insight: Reward-seeking parts of the brain mature earlier than the frontal cortex
brainDevelopment.detail: Frontal cortex (essential for self-control, delay of gratification, resistance to temptation) is not fully developed until mid-20s
brainDevelopment.implication: Preteens are at a particularly vulnerable point in development
